> "By wisdom a house is built, and through understanding it is established." — Proverbs 24:3

## What we kept

The voice. The colors. The flame logo. The Proverbs 27:17 verse at the top of every page. The two product names. The decision to be slow about FaithFlow.

We did not rebuild because the old site was wrong. We rebuilt because it was right, and we wanted to give it room to last.

How Christ Fields collects, uses, and protects your information across the Christ Fields website, GraceFlow, LearnFlow, FaithFlow, and ScholarFlow.
Privacy Policy by Christ Fields
Christ Fields

We collect only what we need to bring you Scripture and run the apps you choose to use.
              In GraceFlow, most of your activity stays on your own device. We never sell your
              information, we run no advertising trackers, and your faith and reflections belong to
              you. This page explains exactly what we gather, why, who helps us run the service, and
              the rights you have over your data.

Christ Fields (“Christ Fields,” “we,” “us”) is a
            Christian technology company based in Colorado, United States. This policy covers the
            Christ Fields website (christfields2717.com), the GraceFlow app, the LearnFlow study
            tier, the FaithFlow community framework, and ScholarFlow. If you have any question about
            your privacy, write to us any time at

Depending on the features you
            use, this can include journal entries, mood check-ins, prayer requests, memory verses,
            progress scores, reading progress, and anything you type into the scripture AI companion.
            Because this content can reveal your religious beliefs and your wellbeing, we treat it as
            sensitive and use it only to provide the service to you, with your consent.
To generate a Scripture response when you use the AI companion.

When you type into the Scripture companion in GraceFlow, the
            text you enter is sent to NVIDIA to generate a Scripture-grounded response. Please do not
            enter information you would not want processed by a third party, such as other
            people’s full names, or financial or medical details. We do not sell what you type,
            and we do not use it to train our own models. NVIDIA processes it under NVIDIA’s own
            terms. A daily limit applies to keep the feature free and available to everyone.

We do not sell your personal information, and we do not share it with advertising
            networks. We use a small set of trusted service providers to run Christ Fields. Each
            handles only what it needs to:
— the AI model behind the Scripture companion.

Once a week the app offers one
            question you may answer in private. Your answer is stored encrypted; we do not read it, no
            leader can see it, only your signed-in account opens it, and you can delete it at any time.
            When you save it, the app looks
            for a theme word (such as “grief” or “work”) using a fixed word list
            on our own server; nothing you write is sent to any outside service or model. You confirm or
            correct that word. Your group’s leaders may then see theme words for the group as a whole,
            never your words, never your name, never a count, and only once at least three people have
            written that fortnight. You can switch even that off on the You page. One exception, for your
            safety: if what you write matches patterns about suicide, self-harm, or being harmed, the app
            shows you the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and sends the leaders of your groups, and
            Christ Fields, one private note that someone needs a person this week, with no words, no
            theme, and no name unless you choose to give it with one tap.

You can choose to connect your Google Calendar in two separate ways, each with its own
            permission screen from Google, and neither is required to use Christ Fields.

With
              the Google permission to manage calendars this app creates, we create one calendar named
              “Christ Fields” in your Google account and place your group’s plans on
              it, updating them when a leader changes or calls something off. This permission does not
              let us see any other calendar or event of yours.

We store the Google token that grants these permissions encrypted, use it only for the two
            purposes above, and never sell, share, or use Google user data for advertising, for
            training models, or for any other purpose. Tap Disconnect on your You page at any time: we
            remove the Christ Fields calendar from your Google account, revoke our access, and delete
            everything we held from Google. You can also remove Christ Fields under Security in your
            Google account. Our use of information received from Google APIs follows the Google API
            Services User Data Policy, including its Limited Use requirements.

Christ Fields services are intended for people aged 13 and older. They are not directed to
            children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone under
            13. If you believe a child under 13 has given us personal information, please contact us at

Christ Fields is operated from the United States, and your information is processed in the
            United States. If you use our services from the European Union or the United Kingdom, you
            have rights under the GDPR and UK GDPR, including access, correction, erasure, restriction,
            portability, and objection. Where we handle sensitive faith or wellbeing content, our
            lawful basis is your explicit consent, which you can withdraw at any time.

As Christ Fields grows, we may update this policy. When we do, we will change the date at
            the top of this page, and for any significant change we will give clearer notice. Please
            check back from time to time.

title: Why we are building Christ Fields
alt: Christ Fields flame logo on dark
Christ Fields is not trying to be a tech company that happens to be Christian.
So we are slow on purpose. We are private on purpose. We are answering to a small list of names, in a small room, where Scripture is opened on a table.
FaithFlow is not an app, a brand, or an online group. It is the Christ Fields community framework for real people walking together in Christ. Scripture-rooted, in-person, and honest.
It is built on a simple truth: you do not grow alone. Accountability, friendship, and faithful community are essential to following Christ.
FaithFlow creates space for people to gather in small groups, study Scripture together, walk through life's challenges with honesty, and sharpen each other in faith and discipline.
Scripture-rooted. The Bible is the foundation, not an afterthought.

Faithful community begins long before you walk in the door. The strongest communities are made of people who already know how to seek Christ on their own.

Use this season to build a foundation. Daily Scripture, honest prayer, and personal discipline. When you step into Iron and Ember, and into a small group within it, you will bring real depth with you.
Read one chapter of the Gospel of John each day for 21 days. Do not rush. Underline what stands out.

Maybe you are sure about Jesus. Maybe you are not sure about any of it yet, and you are simply open. That is enough to begin. This is a place to be honest and to grow, not a place to perform.

This is not about chasing a feeling, or a burst of motivation that fades by Thursday. It is about slowly handing your life over to Christ, the one who already gave his for you. Real change comes from surrender, not from trying harder. We grow into that together.
Whatever you keep track of here stays between you and God. We just walk alongside you. Take your time.
Christ Fields is a small community built on one conviction: that life with Jesus is the realest thing there is, and that we were never meant to walk it alone.
Everything here points to Jesus, not to us and not to your own willpower. He holds all of it together, including you.
You do not have to look like you have it together. God wants truth in the inward being, and so do we. This is a safe place to be real.
There is no condemnation here for those who are in Christ. Missing a day, or a season, never changes how loved you are.
We gather in person. We keep a few honest rhythms. We pray for each other by name. We let Scripture shape how we see things. And we trust God to do the growing, in his time.
God made you, loves you, and came after you in Jesus. His invitation is open and it is for you. You are free to explore it here, at your own pace, with people who are doing the same.
Where did you see God this week, even for a second?
What would you say to God if you were completely honest?
Someone may be carrying a lie they want to put down. Grace before truth lands well.
Anger is in the room for someone. Name it as human before naming it as sin.
Someone is fighting a private battle. Talk about the way out God provides, not the shame.
Pride rarely knows it is pride. Model the lowest seat this week.
Comparison is stealing someone's joy. A word on contentment lands well.
Someone is losing a fight alone. Make it normal to ask for a hand this week.
Someone's mind will not slow down. Rest and the nearness of God are the words.
Fear is close for someone. "Do not be afraid" is the most repeated command for a reason.
Someone is grieving. Leave room for silence; do not rush to the lesson.
Someone feels unseen. Learn a name, ask a second question, sit next to them.
Shame is whispering to someone. Say out loud that there is no condemnation in Christ.
Someone is doubting and afraid to say so. Make doubt speakable this week.
A marriage in the room is under strain. Patience and bearing with one another are the words.
Someone is carrying their children. A word for tired parents lands well.
Family is heavy for someone. Honour and forgiveness both need saying.
A friendship has cracked for someone. Talk about what a brother born for adversity looks like.
Work is weighing on someone. Whom we really work for is the word.
Money is tight for someone. Say plainly that the group helps each other, and how.
Someone's body is failing them. Pray for healing and for grace in weakness, both.
Someone is running on empty. Rest is not a reward; say so.
Someone is asking what it is all for. Talk about faithfulness in the small and ordinary.
Someone doubts they belong. Say who they are to God before what they do for Him.
Someone is deciding whether to forgive. Do not rush it; do not skip it.
Someone is full of thanks. Give it a minute of the room; gratitude is contagious.
Someone wants to pray better and feels behind. Keep it simple and honest.
Church has been complicated for someone. Listen longer than you speak.
A decision is looming for someone. Wisdom, counsel, and peace are the words.
Someone keeps falling in the same place. Talk about the way out, and about company on the way.
Someone is tired of waiting. Waiting on the Lord is different from waiting around; say how.
Hope is thin for someone. The God of hope is the word, not a pep talk.

Some weeks it is Scripture. Some weeks it is a meal, a drive, a climb, a hard conversation. The commitment is to the people, not to the kind of evening. Persistent absence is handled through the correction process, not ignored. If the only thing in the way is a ride, that is not a no — say yes and tell us, because we can usually solve a ride.
The Bible is the inspired Word of God, and the final authority for what I believe and how I live.
“Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness.”
There is one God, eternally existing as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
Jesus Christ is fully God and fully man, and he lived a sinless life.
Jesus died for our sins and rose bodily from the dead.
“Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day.”
Salvation is by grace, through faith in Christ alone, and not something I earn.
“For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works.”
“This Jesus, who was received up from you into the sky, will come back in the same way as you saw him going.”
The Church is the body of Christ, and believers are meant to belong to one another, not to follow him alone.
“Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually.”
Will you submit to the decisions of the Table, except where a decision would require you to act against Scripture?
“We must obey God rather than men.”
Will you verify every Scripture you publish, and put content through the ministry review process before it goes out under the ministry name?
“Give diligence to present yourself approved by God, properly handling the Word of Truth.”
What do your daily prayer and Scripture actually look like right now?
“Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.”
Your co-leader handled something in a way you think was wrong. It was not sin, but you would have done it differently and you think it hurt someone.
In the middle of a study, someone asks you a direct question about the Bible and you genuinely do not know the answer. Everyone is looking at you.
